title: [CQ-M07] Turn on verified-local: starting a worker or QA agent runs it in a Moe VM
definitionOfDone: With executionProfile absent, legacy or observe, launching agents behaves exactly as today; regression tests cover the JetBrains launcher and both wrappers.
With verified-local and readiness met, JetBrains Start Agent for a worker or QA seat runs the CLI inside an owned VM via agent-lifecycle.mjs, and the host never runs that seat's agent CLI. Tested.
With verified-local and readiness not met, Start Agent refuses with a dialog naming each missing capability. No terminal, no VM and no host fallback. Tested.

assertExecutionProfileReady derives readiness from evidence: a passing certify report for this host's platform that matches the current provider version, image pin and supervisor pin, plus the other listed capabilities. Tests prove that no env var, setting, persisted label, caller argument, or report file inside the project or .moe/ satisfies it.
An agent job's changes reach the branch only through export and host admission, then the wrapper's landing. The job's VM is deleted on every exit path, through the owned ledger. Tested.
VS Code reaches parity with the JetBrains launch route and refusal.
Docs are updated: the executionProfile row in CONFIGURATION.md, 'Nothing here is active yet' in ARCHITECTURE.md Local Runner Isolation, and 'Certification is not activation' in CERTIFICATION.md.
One end-to-end task runs on a real VM on Windows and on Linux, run by the human or the governor (not a seat), with the outcome recorded as a task comment.
Daemon npm test, ./gradlew test and node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs pass, run in a git-archive snapshot and not in place in the shared checkout.
taskRails: Never let an env var, setting, persisted label, caller argument or project-supplied file grant verified-local.
Never fall back to running the agent CLI on the host when the VM path fails; refuse instead.
Legacy, the default, stays byte-for-byte unchanged in behavior.
No seat runs Multipass. Real-VM runs belong to the human or the governor.
Do not loosen guest readiness, the certified-provider.json pins or guest-supervisor.py's guarantees.
The open design decisions (VM per job or per seat, the concurrency cap, WSL agent mode, report trust) go to the human before submit_plan.

comments.content:
DESIGN DECISIONS (human, 2026-11-01, architect REPL). Full text: mem:decision-cq-m07-verified-local-activation.
1. VM per SEAT, not per job. Each worker/QA seat gets one owned VM, reused for every job. Between jobs: verified sweep, a NEW root-only supervisor `reset` (materialize refuses an existing workspace), then a fresh materialize. The human accepted /tmp residue across one seat's tasks. The VM is deleted through the owned ledger when the seat exits; cleanup reclaims a crashed seat's VM once the seat is proven gone.
2. Cap derived from host size, host-wide: max(1, min(floor(CPUs/2), floor((RAM-8 GiB)/4 GiB))) agent VMs. Check VMs keep their own dispatch. A seat over the cap waits before claiming, never falls back to the host.
3. WSL mode: under verified-local, worker/QA seats launch natively on Windows (PowerShell + Windows Multipass) whatever the WSL toggle; architect/governor keep WSL; moe-agent.sh refuses verified-local inside WSL.
4. Report trust: host store, live match. Certify files certified reports in <OS account home>/.moe/certification/ (no env override, symlinks refused, nothing inside the project or .moe/). The daemon accepts only native + certified + this host's platform/arch + the LIVE Multipass version + the shipped image and supervisor pins.
5. VM credentials: per-account tokens minted by the accounts CLI into an owner-only store; rotation stays on. codex uses OPENAI_API_KEY/CODEX_API_KEY. gemini/grok are refused under verified-local.
Accepted consequence: the reset mode moves R13's supervisor pin (3a19f3bf), so it is sequenced right after task-fd196d13 and ONE operator re-certify covers both.

comments.author: governor-f668f954
comments.content:
@architect-30d804be The fd196d13 transport design is ruled **APPROVED** (comment-d954b3df), and **Gate 0 passed on both real hosts** (comment-2566639b Windows, comment-888759e9 Linux). Your BACKLOG slices gated on that ruling (e, f, g, h, i, j, m, n) are clear to promote and plan at your pace. What the ruling means for them:
1. **Transport.** Every stdin or bulk stream goes over OpenSSH through guest-ssh.mjs (R14a `sshStreamArgv`) and R14d1/d2/d3's stream runners: materialize, export, verify, the install modes, bridge and check sessions. `multipass exec` stays only for stdin-less queries capped at 64 KiB.
   - M07f's `reset` and M07j's seat job run (materialize, bridge session, export) must reuse that route. Never exec stdio.
   - Your reset is a new supervisor mode, so add it to R14a's frozen `SUPERVISOR_MODES` in the same slice that adds it to guest-supervisor.py main(). The forced command passes any one word, and main()'s allowlist is the gate.
2. **Key custody.** Per-VM SSH keys live in `~/.moe/guest-ssh/<name>.{key,known_hosts}`, not runner-keys (R14a comment-f4d90818). M07g's seat-ledger cleanup must unlink both files when it deletes the VM, the same way R14c's purgeOwned does, and only once the VM is verified absent.
3. **Your stores stay separate.** The certification store (`<home>/.moe/certification/`) and M07k's per-account VM token store must each be their own owner-only directory. Not runner-keys, not guest-ssh, nothing under the project or .moe/.
4. **Pin and certify order.** Per the human's decision, M07f moves the 3a19f3bf pin and one re-certify covers fd196d13 plus M07f. I'll also run an **unrecorded early-signal certify** right after fd196d13 lands, so transport problems surface before M07f. Only the post-M07f run is recorded on R13.
5. **File order.** M07j (and any slice that edits snapshot-transfer.mjs, guest-session.mjs or guest-ssh.mjs) is already behind fd196d13, which depends on every R14 slice. Keep it that way. M07f's guest-supervisor.py edit is free of R14, since no R14 slice touches the supervisor.

comments.author: worker-0e1ab990
comments.content:
CQ-V close-out hand-forward (task-b621ddc9, worker-0e1ab990, 2026-11-01). The CQ-V epic is reviewed end to end. These pieces are built but switched off, and activation must own them:

1. Nothing invokes the trusted runner's check client (scripts/local-runner/check-dispatch.mjs, V04b) per strong candidate. Required checks are only ever recorded by tests.
2. Trusted-install provisioning of `moe-daemon check-architecture` is unbuilt. Only that installed form counts: anything else reports required-check-untrusted-checker:<id> (efbf1742). The --rules config files need protection too.
3. check-architecture judges a committed --tree against its first parent, so the candidate must be materialized as a single commit on baseRevision (comment-5381881a on V10).
4. Protection covers only the entries the approver names. A protected wrapper that runs unprotected candidate code (a dist built from candidate sources, a helper or a package script) is outside it (comment-bde17873, V01).
5. NEW: task-5464e725 (MEDIUM). Guest-session STAMPED never stamps attemptId/generation/sessionId onto qa_approve/qa_reject, so a VM QA seat is always refused STEP_ENTRY_IDENTITY_REQUIRED under verified-local. Suggest adding it to this row's dependsOn: it fails closed, but it blocks the QA VM route. M07j1's design assumes the parity.
6. Display note for the readiness/clients slices: a strong task that owes no check shows requiredCheckSatisfied absent (documented "no check owed"), while qa_approve refuses with required-checks-undeclared.
